texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Abstract
texts.text: Abstract

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Optimising ESP runlife is essential to avoid additional workover costs and maintain production levels. Although some failures may require specialist equipment or solutions, the vast majority of short runlives are preventable. These problems usually result from a lack of consideration of the entire ESP system during the design phase or shortcomings during the installation and operations phases.
texts.text: Optimising ESP runlife is essential to avoid additional workover costs and maintain production levels. Although some failures may require specialist equipment or solutions, the vast majority of short runlives are preventable. These problems usually result from a lack of consideration of the entire ESP system during the design phase or shortcomings during the installation and operations phases.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This paper will examine the most common causes of premature ESP system failure and identify the reasons and possible solutions for the problem. A checklist has been devised to assist new or existing users of ESPs to design, install and operate an ESP system to achieve and optimum runlife for particular well conditions.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Introduction
texts.text: Introduction

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In many areas of the world where ESPs are being newly introduced a common concern among users is the potential for premature failures, thus rendering the economic benefit of ESPs vs. other lift methods (higher production rates) null and void. Many companies will avoid the use of ESPs until all other possibilities are exhausted, primarily due to this fear of the unknown and perceived unreliability of ESP systems.
texts.text: In many areas of the world where ESPs are being newly introduced a common concern among users is the potential for premature failures, thus rendering the economic benefit of ESPs vs. other lift methods (higher production rates) null and void. Many companies will avoid the use of ESPs until all other possibilities are exhausted, primarily due to this fear of the unknown and perceived unreliability of ESP systems.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In fact, the volume of experience with ESPs in a huge variety of applications and conditions is such that most problems have been identified and are readily fixed. In other words, the 'learning curve' has already been learnt and there is no reason that this expertise should not widely applied - especially for the benefit of new users.
texts.text: In fact, the volume of experience with ESPs in a huge variety of applications and conditions is such that most problems have been identified and are readily fixed. In other words, the 'learning curve' has already been learnt and there is no reason that this expertise should not widely applied - especially for the benefit of new users.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most failures  of  ESPs  are  electrical  in  nature,  since  this  is  the  lifeline  that  provides  energy  to  the motor and pump and is often the weakest link of the system. However, the real cause of failure could be elsewhere (such as reservoir inflow plugging or a valve shut at surface causing motor and pump heating) and a proper cause and effect analysis should always be conducted.

The use of a practical checklist will be reviewed to show how virtually all issues and problems that effect runlife have easily implemented solutions.

texts.orig: Background
texts.text: Background

texts.label: text
texts.orig: An ESP system is made up of five principal components:
texts.text: An ESP system is made up of five principal components:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 1) a multistage centrifugal pump consisting of rotating impellers and fixed diffusers
texts.text: a multistage centrifugal pump consisting of rotating impellers and fixed diffusers

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 3) a seal section which isolates well fluids from the motor and accommodates shaft movement
texts.text: a seal section which isolates well fluids from the motor and accommodates shaft movement

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 2) a high speed ( ≈ 3500 rpm) three-phase electric motor filled with dielectric oil
texts.text: a high speed ( ≈ 3500 rpm) three-phase electric motor filled with dielectric oil

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 4) a three conductor electric cable which runs through the wellhead down to the motor
texts.text: a three conductor electric cable which runs through the wellhead down to the motor

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 5) a power supply system at surface (generator, transformer, variable frequency drive)
texts.text: a power supply system at surface (generator, transformer, variable frequency drive)

texts.text: the diffuser converts fluid energy (hydraulic kinetic) to potential energy

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: The Problems
texts.text: The Problems

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Failure  modes  in  ESP  systems  result  from  one  or  a  combination  of  factors  that  compromise  the operation of each component. Since the principles of operation of each component is known, then the causes of failure in each can easily be identified:
texts.text: Failure  modes  in  ESP  systems  result  from  one  or  a  combination  of  factors  that  compromise  the operation of each component. Since the principles of operation of each component is known, then the causes of failure in each can easily be identified:

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: The pump
texts.text: The pump

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The high fluid velocities through the impeller vanes in a pump stage give rise to several problems related to frictional pressure losses:
texts.text: The high fluid velocities through the impeller vanes in a pump stage give rise to several problems related to frictional pressure losses:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · gas bubbles greater than the impeller vane size results in cavitation and gas-locking
texts.text: gas bubbles greater than the impeller vane size results in cavitation and gas-locking

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · sand or scale causes erosional wear and/or plugging of the impeller vanes and pump intake
texts.text: sand or scale causes erosional wear and/or plugging of the impeller vanes and pump intake

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · high viscosity fluids lower efficiency of energy conversion due to higher friction
texts.text: high viscosity fluids lower efficiency of energy conversion due to higher friction

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · any wellbore debris sucked into the pump will result in blocking or damage to the stages
texts.text: any wellbore debris sucked into the pump will result in blocking or damage to the stages

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Operation out of the range of the pump (too little or too much flow ) also causes problems due to low efficiency (giving rise to heating ) and mechanical wear between the impellers and diffusers.
texts.text: Operation out of the range of the pump (too little or too much flow ) also causes problems due to low efficiency (giving rise to heating ) and mechanical wear between the impellers and diffusers.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Initial sizing of the pump is done by determination of average flowrate in the pump (rb/d) and total dynamic head (TDH) required. These depend primarily on the well inflow performance (productivity index and reservoir pressure) and fluid properties (mainly density and viscosity). If either of these design input assumptions is  incorrect, then the pump design is wrongly specified and early failure could result.
texts.text: Initial sizing of the pump is done by determination of average flowrate in the pump (rb/d) and total dynamic head (TDH) required. These depend primarily on the well inflow performance (productivity index and reservoir pressure) and fluid properties (mainly density and viscosity). If either of these design input assumptions is  incorrect, then the pump design is wrongly specified and early failure could result.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: The seal/protector section
texts.text: The seal/protector section

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The seal section is generally quite robust, but failure could occur due to the following:
texts.text: The seal section is generally quite robust, but failure could occur due to the following:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · very high shaft load caused by operation out of range of pump (up/downthrust)
texts.text: very high shaft load caused by operation out of range of pump (up/downthrust)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · operation at extreme temperature or fast pressure changes resulting in seal failure
texts.text: operation at extreme temperature or fast pressure changes resulting in seal failure

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · high shaft vibration due to debris or wear in pump
texts.text: high shaft vibration due to debris or wear in pump

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · operation at high angles with labyrinth type seals
texts.text: operation at high angles with labyrinth type seals

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: The electrical system
texts.text: The electrical system

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Since the electrical system is simply a series circuit, any component that is the weakest link will result in system failure. Common problems include:
texts.text: Since the electrical system is simply a series circuit, any component that is the weakest link will result in system failure. Common problems include:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · damage to any component due transportation, handling or installation
texts.text: damage to any component due transportation, handling or installation

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · lack of heat transfer medium around the motor (i.e. gas build-up)
texts.text: lack of heat transfer medium around the motor (i.e. gas build-up)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · extreme heating of the cable or motor (due to low flow, operation out of pump range etc.)
texts.text: extreme heating of the cable or motor (due to low flow, operation out of pump range etc.)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · high shaft thrust or loading due to a pump problem (out of range, gas cavitation, wear etc.)
texts.text: high shaft thrust or loading due to a pump problem (out of range, gas cavitation, wear etc.)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · use of a single inferior component in any part of the electrical system
texts.text: use of a single inferior component in any part of the electrical system

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · operation with unclean power supply (i.e. voltage spiking or fluctuations, harmonics etc.)
texts.text: operation with unclean power supply (i.e. voltage spiking or fluctuations, harmonics etc.)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Operational problems can also give rise to premature electrical failures, e.g. shut-in of surface or subsurface  safety  valve  with  the  ESP  running,  plugging  of  perforations  or  pump  intake,  downhole recirculation etc.
texts.text: Operational problems can also give rise to premature electrical failures, e.g. shut-in of surface or subsurface  safety  valve  with  the  ESP  running,  plugging  of  perforations  or  pump  intake,  downhole recirculation etc.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: The Solutions
texts.text: The Solutions

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A systematic examination of each of the failures modes above leads to the following solutions that either  eliminate  or  accommodate  the  problem  through  proper  equipment  selection  or  improved installation  procedures  and  operations  practices.  Some  examples  for  the  most  common  issues  are given below - a full set of solutions is given in the attached checklist .
texts.text: A systematic examination of each of the failures modes above leads to the following solutions that either  eliminate  or  accommodate  the  problem  through  proper  equipment  selection  or  improved installation  procedures  and  operations  practices.  Some  examples  for  the  most  common  issues  are given below - a full set of solutions is given in the attached checklist .

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Gas handling
texts.text: Gas handling

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Gas is a very common issue with ESP systems, but problems can be avoided by consideration of the following during the design phase:
texts.text: Gas is a very common issue with ESP systems, but problems can be avoided by consideration of the following during the design phase:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · set the pump as deep as possible (to raise pump intake pressures)
texts.text: set the pump as deep as possible (to raise pump intake pressures)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · install a gas handler (no venting required) - up to 60% free gas at intake
texts.text: install a gas handler (no venting required) - up to 60% free gas at intake

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · use large, mixed flow impellers (bigger vane size than radial flow) - up to 30% free gas
texts.text: use large, mixed flow impellers (bigger vane size than radial flow) - up to 30% free gas

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · install a gas separator (requiring venting up the annulus) - up to 80% free gas at intake
texts.text: install a gas separator (requiring venting up the annulus) - up to 80% free gas at intake

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · avoid tight clearances around motor (to avoid annular gas build-up)
texts.text: avoid tight clearances around motor (to avoid annular gas build-up)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · use axial flow impellers (requires use of hydraulic submersible pump) - up to 80% free gas
texts.text: use axial flow impellers (requires use of hydraulic submersible pump) - up to 80% free gas

texts.label: text
texts.orig: During the operational phase, i.e. once the ESP has been run, consider the following:
texts.text: During the operational phase, i.e. once the ESP has been run, consider the following:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · increase wellhead pressure by choking the well (raises intake pressure)
texts.text: increase wellhead pressure by choking the well (raises intake pressure)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · lower ESP supply frequency (raises intake pressure)
texts.text: lower ESP supply frequency (raises intake pressure)

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: High viscosity fluids
texts.text: High viscosity fluids

texts.label: text
texts.orig: High viscosity oils or emulsions can be handled by the following design phase considerations:
texts.text: High viscosity oils or emulsions can be handled by the following design phase considerations:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · use large, mixed flow impellers (bigger vane size than radial flow) - less friction
texts.text: use large, mixed flow impellers (bigger vane size than radial flow) - less friction

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · add means to inject demulsifier at pump intake (e.g. capillary line)
texts.text: add means to inject demulsifier at pump intake (e.g. capillary line)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · design for lower rpm with more stages - lowers friction
texts.text: design for lower rpm with more stages - lowers friction

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · for extremely high viscosities, use a progressive cavity pump (PCP)
texts.text: for extremely high viscosities, use a progressive cavity pump (PCP)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: During the operational phase, consider the following:
texts.text: During the operational phase, consider the following:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · lower ESP supply frequency (to lower rpm and hence friction)
texts.text: lower ESP supply frequency (to lower rpm and hence friction)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · inject demulsifier at pump intake
texts.text: inject demulsifier at pump intake

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Sand, scale or debris
texts.text: Sand, scale or debris

texts.label: text
texts.orig: These are common contaminants of ESP systems and can be handled during the design , installation and operational phases as follows:
texts.text: These are common contaminants of ESP systems and can be handled during the design , installation and operational phases as follows:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · prevent sand influx in the first place, by use of a gravel pack or screens
texts.text: prevent sand influx in the first place, by use of a gravel pack or screens

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · clean out wellbore prior to ESP installation
texts.text: clean out wellbore prior to ESP installation

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · inject scale inhibitor at pump intake or periodically scale squeeze
texts.text: inject scale inhibitor at pump intake or periodically scale squeeze

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · use large, mixed flow impellers (bigger vane size than radial flow)
texts.text: use large, mixed flow impellers (bigger vane size than radial flow)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · use a special pump design for sand (upgraded metallurgy, radial wear protection etc.)
texts.text: use a special pump design for sand (upgraded metallurgy, radial wear protection etc.)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · start up pump slowly to prevent ingestion of sand/debris
texts.text: start up pump slowly to prevent ingestion of sand/debris

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: The electrical system
texts.text: The electrical system

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As the electrical system is the most common immediate cause of failure, particular attention should be paid to the following:
texts.text: As the electrical system is the most common immediate cause of failure, particular attention should be paid to the following:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · ensure a clean power supply system (especially if using variable frequency drives)
texts.text: ensure a clean power supply system (especially if using variable frequency drives)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · upgrade installation procedures (time for splice, slow run in hole, use cable clamps etc)
texts.text: upgrade installation procedures (time for splice, slow run in hole, use cable clamps etc)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · use top quality components throughout the electrical system
texts.text: use top quality components throughout the electrical system

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: An Integrated Approach
texts.text: An Integrated Approach

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When optimising  the  reliability  and  hence  runlife  of  ESP  systems,  it  is  essential  to  take  a  whole system or integrated approach. This will avoid overlooking any element that could be the weak link of the system that causes premature failure. Some guidelines to this approach are given below.
texts.text: When optimising  the  reliability  and  hence  runlife  of  ESP  systems,  it  is  essential  to  take  a  whole system or integrated approach. This will avoid overlooking any element that could be the weak link of the system that causes premature failure. Some guidelines to this approach are given below.

texts.orig: A fully instrumented ESP system with appropriate alarms and trips set can prevent many of the most common failure modes, without operator intervention. More subtle problems require careful analysis and interpretation of all parameters (e.g. determination of viscosity effect on pump performance).

texts.orig: Conclusions
texts.text: Conclusions

texts.label: text
texts.orig: ESPs  are  a  reliable,  high-rate  artificial  lift  system.  Most  failures  are  preventable  with  readily identifiable causes. These failures can be avoided by following a systematic, integrated approach to the entire ESP system in the design, installation and operational phases of a field development.
texts.text: ESPs  are  a  reliable,  high-rate  artificial  lift  system.  Most  failures  are  preventable  with  readily identifiable causes. These failures can be avoided by following a systematic, integrated approach to the entire ESP system in the design, installation and operational phases of a field development.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Monitoring  of  an  ESP  system  is  essential  to  protect  against  obvious  failure  modes  and  to  provide critical data to allow more complex problems to be solved. A problem cannot be fixed unless it is first identified and the cause determined.
